mainTopic: How far a כהן and other witnesses are trusted about a blemished בכור
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier point: רבי מאיר's suspicion of כהנים is only a worry, not a firm label. The גמרא then rules that hearsay testimony (עד מפי עד) is valid for a blemished בכור, following רב אשי's reading of a ברייתא. Next, רבי אילעא teaches that a כהן who alone reveals that an animal is a בכור is believed that its blemish came naturally. The גמרא explains why this ruling was needed, and it rejects מר בר רב אשי's comparison to a rented donkey by separating a certain fact from a mere worry. A long story follows about רבי צדוק's בכור. רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל disagree about whether a learned כהן is trusted more, and the people protest when רבי יהושע is left standing. A new משנה then rules that a כהן is believed when he says an expert saw his בכור. רב adds that a כהן is believed when he says he received the animal already blemished, because people do not lie about what can be checked. רב שיזבי challenges this rule from a case about מעשר, and the answer, which begins with 'it is different there,' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's suspicion is only a concern
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier difficulty: רבי מאיר only treats כהנים as a possible worry, not as people who definitely cause blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say that רבי מאיר spoke about suspicion only as a concern. Did he say it to establish them as definitely doing it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer to a question from the previous section. It explains that רבי מאיר's suspicion of כהנים is a worry, not a firm label.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of suspicion. One level is a concern that someone might have done something wrong. The other level is treating him as someone who definitely does it. רבי מאיר only meant the first level, so the earlier difficulty that assumed the second level goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: One can say (introduces a possible answer)
To establish them as (definitely) being that way
Did he say? (a rhetorical question that means 'certainly not')

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'מי אמר' looks like a real question, but it is rhetorical. It means 'he certainly did not say that.'

phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Meir said it as a concern,
phrases.notes: He meant only a worry that the כהן might have caused the blemish.

phrases.english: but did he say it to establish them [as definite offenders]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised earlier about רבי מאיר's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing levels of suspicion (concern versus established status)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר treats כהנים as people who definitely cause blemishes.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר only means there is a concern, which is weaker than an established status.

steps.title: Is hearsay testimony valid for a firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is raised about whether עד מפי עד is accepted for a בכור's blemish. רב אסי forbids it and רב אשי permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the law of a witness repeating another witness's words, for testimony about a בכור? רב אסי forbids, and רב אשי permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new topic. It asks whether hearsay testimony works for a blemished בכור, and two אמוראים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a witness must testify about what he himself saw. Here someone only repeats what another witness told him. The question is whether that is enough to allow slaughtering a בכור because it has a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
A witness repeating another witness (hearsay testimony)
Firstborn animal, which may be slaughtered outside the מקדש only if it has a blemish

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
A witness from the mouth of a witness (hearsay),
what is [the law] for testimony about a firstborn?
Rav Asi forbids,
and Rav Ashi permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עֵד מִפִּי עֵד, מַהוּ לְעֵדוּת בְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hearsay testimony is enough to establish that a בכור has a blemish.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב אסי (who forbids) with רב אשי (who permits). The names look almost the same.

steps.title: Challenge from the school of מנשה
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי challenges רב אשי from a ברייתא saying hearsay is valid only for a woman's testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said to רב אשי: But the school of מנשה taught that hearsay testimony is valid only for the testimony of a woman!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי attacks the lenient opinion with a ברייתא. The ברייתא seems to limit hearsay to one single case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי reads 'עדות האשה' as the case of testifying that a woman's husband died so that she may remarry. If hearsay works only there, it should not work for a בכור. That would make רב אשי wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught? (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
Testimony about a woman (that her husband died)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַסִּי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said to Rav Ashi:
But didn't the school of Menashe teach:
Hearsay testimony is not valid
except for the testimony of a woman!
phrases.notes: Meaning testimony that her husband died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's lenient position from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's ruling that hearsay is valid for a בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits hearsay to one case (a woman's testimony about her husband's death), so it should not be valid for a בכור.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא differently
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the ברייתא as: hearsay is valid for any testimony where a woman is a valid witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it this way: only for testimony in which a woman is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by changing how the ברייתא should be read. The answer now supports his view instead of contradicting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי read 'עדות האשה' as testimony about a woman. רב אשי reads it as testimony that a woman herself can give. Wherever a woman's testimony is accepted, hearsay is accepted too. Since a woman may testify about a בכור's blemish, hearsay works for a בכור.
steps.confusionAlert: 'תני' does not mean someone made a mistake in copying. It tells us to read the ברייתא with a different meaning: 'testimony a woman can give,' not 'testimony about a woman.'

phrases.english: Teach [it like this]:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְעֵדוּת שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁרָה לָהּ בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: only for testimony for which a woman is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנִי: אֶלָּא לְעֵדוּת שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁרָה לָהּ בִּלְבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's challenge from step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא limits hearsay to testimony about a woman's husband's death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows hearsay in every case where a woman's testimony is valid, and that includes a בכור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rereading turns the ברייתא into a general rule. It also sets up the final הלכה.

steps.title: רב יימר permits, and מרימר mocks him
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר accepted hearsay testimony for a בכור. מרימר nicknamed him 'יימר who permits firstborns.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר accepted hearsay testimony for a בכור. מרימר called him: 'יימר permits firstborns.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of a real ruling following the lenient view. It also records that מרימר disapproved of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יימר actually ruled like רב אשי in practice. מרימר's nickname shows he thought this was too lenient. In his view, רב יימר was letting people eat בכורות too easily.

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar deemed valid
hearsay testimony for a firstborn;
Mareimar called him:
"Yeimar permits firstborns."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יֵימַר אַכְשַׁר עֵד מִפִּי עֵד בִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical ruling that follows רב אשי, along with criticism of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יימר accepted hearsay testimony for a בכור, and מרימר criticized him for it.

steps.title: Final ruling: hearsay is valid for a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that עד מפי עד is valid for testimony about a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: hearsay testimony is valid for testimony about a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling. It follows רב אשי and רב יימר, not מרימר's criticism.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though מרימר disapproved, the הלכה follows the lenient view. Hearsay testimony may be relied on to show that a בכור's blemish is acceptable.
steps.whatToRemember: עד מפי עד is valid for a בכור. This follows רב אשי's reading of the ברייתא: hearsay works wherever a woman's testimony works.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
hearsay testimony is valid
for testimony about a firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: עֵד מִפִּי עֵד כָּשֵׁר לְעֵדוּת בְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the הלכה after the story about מרימר's criticism.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Hearsay testimony is accepted for a blemished בכור, following רב אשי.

steps.title: A כהן is believed about an unknown בכור and its blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא rules that when no one knew an animal was a בכור, a כהן who says 'it is a בכור and it already has its blemish' is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: If people did not know that this animal was a בכור, and someone came and said, 'It is a בכור, and its blemish is with it,' he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אילעא. A כהן is trusted when he reports that an animal is a בכור and that it already has a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בכור with a blemish raises a worry: maybe the כהן made the blemish himself so he could eat it. Here, though, the only reason anyone knows it is a בכור at all is that the כהן said so. So we trust the rest of what he says too, including that the blemish happened naturally.

keyTerms.meaning: Known or established (here: no one knew the animal was a בכור)
Its blemish is with it, meaning the blemish came about by itself

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מוּחְזָקִין בּוֹ שֶׁהוּא בְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: If they did not know it to be a firstborn,
phrases.notes: No one knew this animal was a בכור.

phrases.english: and one person came and said that it is a firstborn
and its blemish is with it, he is believed.
phrases.notes: The blemish was not made on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related ruling about trusting testimony for a בכור. It follows the conclusion that hearsay is accepted for a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the animal was not known to be a בכור, the person who reports that it is a בכור with a natural blemish is believed.

steps.title: Why say this? The משנה already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אילעא adds. The rule הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר is already taught in a משנה about a woman who says she was married and is now divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted? We already learned that in a משנה: a woman who said 'I was a married woman, and I am divorced' is believed, because the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אילעא's ruling as unnecessary. It seems to repeat a rule we already know from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The principle of הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר works like this: if the only source of a prohibition is a person's own words, we also believe him when he says it is permitted. The משנה applies this to a woman who reports both her marriage and her divorce. So the גמרא asks why רבי אילעא needed to state the same idea for a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asks what new point a statement makes)
The mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted
We already learned it (in a משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on whether רבי אילעא's ruling is correct. The גמרא agrees with the ruling. It is only asking why he needed to say it at all.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
That the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted?
We already learned: a woman who said,
'I was a married woman, and I am divorced,' is believed,
because the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אילעא's ruling as repeating what we already know.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems to repeat the known principle הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר, already taught in the משנה about the woman who says she is divorced.

steps.title: The בכור case is different, but the כהן is still believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the בכור case needs its own ruling. The woman did not have to speak at all, but the כהן has to reveal that the animal is a בכור. Still, he is believed, because a cheater would simply have made an obvious blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there, she is believed because if she wanted, she could have said nothing at all. But here, he has no choice but to say it, because he will not eat קדשים outside the Temple. So I would say this is not a case of 'the mouth that forbade.' He teaches us otherwise: if that were his plan, he would have made an obvious blemish on it and eaten it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows a reason we might have thought the כהן is not believed, and then explains why he is believed anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the possible mistake (הוה אמינא): the woman could have stayed quiet, so her words truly create the prohibition. The כהן, though, must tell an expert it is a בכור, since he cannot rule on the blemish himself and will not risk eating קדשים בחוץ. So his words might not count as freely 'forbidding.' The conclusion: we still trust him, because a cheating כהן would have made a blemish that everyone can see, and then he would not have needed to speak at all.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a possible but wrong assumption)
There is no way to avoid (he has no choice but to)
Eating sacrificial meat outside the Temple, which is punished with כרת
An obvious blemish that everyone can see

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן who alone reveals that an animal is a בכור is believed that its blemish came naturally. This holds even though he had to come forward, because a cheater would have made an obvious blemish instead.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the structure. Everything from מהו דתימא until קא משמע לן is the wrong assumption we might have made. Only the words after קא משמע לן give the actual conclusion.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר still applies even when the speaker was under some pressure to speak, as long as he had an easier way to cheat that he did not use.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּאִי בָּעֲיָא לָא אָמְרָה.
phrases.english: It is only there, since if she wanted, she would not have said it.
phrases.notes: The woman could have stayed silent and remarried.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּלָא סַגִּיא דְּלָא אָמְרָה,
phrases.english: But here, where he has no choice but to say it,
since he would not eat sacrificial meat outside,
phrases.notes: He must show it to an expert, so he must reveal that it is a בכור.

phrases.english: I would say: this is not a case of 'the mouth that forbade,'
so he teaches us,
that if it were for that reason (to cheat),
he would have put an obvious blemish on it
and eaten it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by showing what new point רבי אילעא's ruling teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (צריכותא): shows why the בכור case needed its own statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the כהן is forced to reveal that it is a בכור (he cannot eat קדשים בחוץ), his words would not count as הפה שאסר, so he would not be believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is believed, because a cheater would have made an obvious blemish and eaten it without needing to reveal anything.

steps.title: A challenge from the case of the rented donkey
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי asks how רבי אילעא's ruling differs from a case where a man rented out his donkey. The owner told the renter not to take the watery road of נהר פקוד. The renter took that road anyway, the donkey died, and he claimed there was no water.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי objected: How is this different from a certain man who rented his donkey to his friend? He told him: 'Do not go on the road of נהר פקוד, where there is water. Go on the road of נרש, where there is no water.' The renter went on the road of נהר פקוד and the donkey died. He came back and said: 'I did go on the road of נהר פקוד, but there was no water.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי starts a challenge against רבי אילעא's ruling by telling a case about a rented donkey. The step is setting up the challenge, and the ruling on this case comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the donkey case, the renter admits he broke the owner's instructions, but he claims nothing dangerous happened. This is like the כהן, who admits it is a בכור but claims the blemish came on its own. If the renter is not believed, maybe the כהן should not be believed either.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it. This opens a challenge.
What is the difference? This compares two cases.
A road with water, which is dangerous for a donkey

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi objected to it:
What is different from that man
who rented a donkey to his friend,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא תֵּיזִיל בְּאוֹרְחָא דִּנְהַר פְּקוֹד
phrases.english: and said to him: Do not go on the road of Nehar Pekod
where there is water;
go on the road of Neresh, where there is no water.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל בְּאוֹרְחָא דִּנְהַר פְּקוֹד וּמִית חֲמָרָא,
phrases.english: He went on the road of Nehar Pekod and the donkey died.
He came and said to him:
I went on the road of Nehar Pekod,
but there was no water.
phrases.notes: So, he claims, the water did not cause the death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of Step 9 that the כהן is believed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's ruling that the כהן is believed about the blemish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a similar case where a person admits a fact against himself and offers an innocent explanation. If he is not believed there, the כהן should not be believed here.

steps.title: רבא and אביי rule on the donkey case
steps.stepSummary: רבא said the renter is believed because of מה לו לשקר: he could have lied and said he took the road of נרש. אביי answered that we do not say מה לו לשקר in a place where witnesses can check.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why would he lie? If he wanted to lie, he could have said: 'I went on the road of נרש.' אביי said: We do not say 'why would he lie' in a place where there are witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge by quoting the ruling on the donkey case. אביי's rule, that מה לו לשקר does not work when witnesses can establish the facts, is the point the challenge relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows the road of נהר פקוד has water, so the renter's 'better lie' argument cannot beat a known fact. The challenge is that it is also 'known' that כהנים are suspected of making blemishes. So the כהן's מה לו לשקר should not help him either.

keyTerms.meaning: Why would he lie? He is believed because he could have made a better false claim.
In a place where there are witnesses, meaning the facts are known or can be checked

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying actual witnesses came to court. He means the fact, that this road has water, is publicly known, so it acts like witnesses.

phrases.english: And Rava said: Why would he lie?

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי אָמַר: בְּאוֹרְחָא דְּנַרֶשׁ אֲזַלִי.
phrases.english: If he wanted, he could have said: I went on the road of Neresh.
And Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: ״מָה לוֹ לְשַׁקֵּר״ בִּמְקוֹם עֵדִים לָא אָמְרִינַן.
phrases.english: 'Why would he lie' we do not say in a place of witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from Step 10 by giving the ruling on the donkey case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of מה לו לשקר in Step 9 to believe the כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי rules that מה לו לשקר does not work against a known fact. Since כהנים are known to be suspected, the כהן's argument should fail as well.

steps.title: The cases are different: certainty versus a mere worry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. On the road of נהר פקוד there is certainly water. With the בכור, it is not certain the כהן made a blemish. It is only a worry, and against a worry we do say מה לו לשקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, there is certainly water. Here, is it certain that he put a blemish in it? It is only a worry, and where there is only a worry, we do say 'why would he lie.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away מר בר רב אשי's challenge by showing that the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's rule only applies when the opposing fact is certain, like the known water on that road. Suspicion that a כהן made a blemish is only a possibility, not a known fact. So מה לו לשקר still works, and רבי אילעא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? This phrase rejects a comparison.
A worry or suspicion, not a certainty

steps.whatToRemember: מה לו לשקר does not work against a known fact. It does work against a mere suspicion. Because of this, the כהן is believed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit of מה לו לשקר: certainty versus suspicion. The distinction is useful wherever this argument comes up.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, there is certainly water;
here, did he certainly put a blemish in it?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. The answer is no.

phrases.english: It is only a worry,
and in a place of worry we do say 'why would he lie.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in Steps 10-11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the donkey case and the בכור case, not אביי's rule itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge treated a mere suspicion as if it were a known certainty.

steps.title: Who said this ruling: it belongs to רבי אילעא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא was teaching this ruling without naming who said it. רבא זוטי told him: we learn it in the name of רבי אילעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was sitting and saying this teaching without naming the person who said it. רבא זוטי said to רבינא: We learn it in the name of רבי אילעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short note about who said the ruling: it is רבי אילעא's teaching, not an unnamed one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step does not change the law. It only fixes the source. A ruling taught with no name could sound like it is accepted by everyone, so naming רבי אילעא shows it is his own statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Without a man, meaning taught with no name attached

phrases.english: Ravina was sitting and saying
this teaching without a name.
Rava Zuti said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אִילְעָא מַתְנִינַן לַהּ.
phrases.english: We learn it in the name of Rabbi Ile'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רָבִינָא וְקָאָמַר לְהַאי שְׁמַעְתָּא בְּלָא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רבי אילעא section by naming who said the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling about believing the כהן is taught in the name of רבי אילעא.

steps.title: רבי צדוק's firstborn splits its lip
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק had a בכור. He put barley in wicker baskets for it, and while it ate, its lip split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי צדוק had a בכור. He put barley in baskets for it. While it was eating, its lip split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a כהן whose בכור got a blemish. The step only sets up the facts, and the question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A split lip is a blemish that lets a בכור be eaten outside the Temple. The blemish happened while the animal was eating, so it could have been an accident. But a כהן who caused it would gain from it, so there is a question of whether רבי צדוק is suspected.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tzadok had a firstborn animal.
He put barley in baskets for it.
While it was eating, its lip split.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about a כהן's credibility when a בכור gets a blemish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The facts of the case: a בכור got a blemish in a way that may have been an accident.

steps.title: רבי צדוק asks whether a learned כהן is treated differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק came before רבי יהושע and asked: Did we not make a distinction between a חבר and an עם הארץ?
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבי יהושע and said to him: Did we make any distinction between a חבר and an עם הארץ?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי צדוק asks רבי יהושע whether a learned כהן is believed more than an unlearned one, so that his word about this blemish could be accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary כהן may be suspected of making blemishes on purpose. רבי צדוק wants to know if a חבר, a careful and learned person, is trusted to say the blemish was an accident.

keyTerms.meaning: A learned person who is careful in observance
An unlearned person who is not careful in observance

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Yehoshua,
and said to him: Did we make any distinction
between a learned person and an unlearned person?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם חִילַּקְנוּ בֵּין חָבֵר לְעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the legal question that comes out of the facts in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a חבר כהן is believed about a בכור's blemish when an עם הארץ would not be

steps.title: רבי יהושע answers: yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answered yes: a distinction is made, so רבי צדוק, as a חבר, is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers that yes, a חבר is treated differently from an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A learned, careful כהן is trusted to say the blemish was an accident. So רבי צדוק's בכור is treated as having a real blemish that came on its own.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, a חבר is distinguished from an עם הארץ and is believed.

steps.title: רבי צדוק asks רבן גמליאל the same question
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק brings his question to רבן גמליאל: do we make a distinction between a חבר and an עם הארץ?
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבן גמליאל and said to him: Did we make a distinction between a חבר and an עם הארץ?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי צדוק already got an answer from רבי יהושע. Now he asks the same question to רבן גמליאל, the head of the academy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע had said a חבר is believed that his בכור's blemish happened by itself. רבי צדוק now checks this with the highest authority. This sets up a clash between the two rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: The נשיא (head) of the academy in Yavne at that time

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Tzadok) came before Rabban Gamliel,
he said to him:
Did we make a distinction between a chaver and an am ha'aretz?
phrases.notes: About being believed that a blemish on a בכור happened by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, אָמַר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question from Step 15, now to a second authority.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a חבר is believed more than an עם הארץ about a blemish on a בכור.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל answers no
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל rules that no distinction is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers that we do not make a distinction between a חבר and an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of what רבי יהושע said in Step 16. According to רבן גמליאל, even a חבר is not believed here, so רבי צדוק's בכור would not be allowed.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17, contradicting רבי יהושע's answer in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No distinction: a חבר is not believed more than an עם הארץ.

steps.title: But רבי יהושע told me yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק pushes back: רבי יהושע told him that a distinction is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But רבי יהושע told me yes!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי צדוק challenges רבן גמליאל by quoting the opposite ruling he heard from רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now two great rabbis have given opposite rulings. רבי צדוק points out the conflict and implicitly asks which one is right.

phrases.english: He said to him: But surely
phrases.notes: The printed text reads והא; the corrected reading is והלא. Both mean 'but surely.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua told me yes!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר לִי הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 18 using Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's ruling that no distinction is made
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another leading authority, רבי יהושע, ruled the opposite.

steps.title: Wait until the scholars come to the study hall
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל delays his answer until the scholars gather in the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wait until the 'shield-bearers' come up to the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל does not answer right away. He sets up a public discussion for when all the scholars arrive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of settling it privately, רבן גמליאל wants to deal with the question in front of all the scholars. 'Shield-bearers' means the Torah scholars, who 'fight' in the battle of Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Masters of the shields. A name for the Torah scholars who debate

phrases.english: He said to him: Wait
until the masters of the shields (the scholars) go up
to the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְתֵּן עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלוּ בַּעֲלֵי תְרִיסִין לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to Step 19 by delaying and setting up the public scene.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No direct answer. The issue will be raised publicly in the בית המדרש.

steps.title: The question is asked publicly
steps.stepSummary: In the בית המדרש, the questioner stands and asks the same question in front of everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they entered the בית המדרש, the questioner stood and asked: Did we make any distinction between a חבר and an עם הארץ?
steps.whatsHappening: The scene moves to the full study hall. The same question is now asked in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are almost the same as Step 17, but now רבי יהושע is in the room. This sets up a direct face-to-face test of his earlier ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Did we at all...? (strengthens the question)

phrases.english: Once they entered the study hall,
the questioner stood up and asked:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם חִילַּקְנוּ בֵּין חָבֵר לְעַם הָאָרֶץ?
phrases.english: Did we make any distinction between a chaver and an am ha'aretz?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the plan from Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The same question, now asked publicly with רבי יהושע present.

steps.title: רבי יהושע says no
steps.stepSummary: In public, רבי יהושע answers that no distinction is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers 'no' in public, which is the opposite of what he told רבי צדוק privately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now his public answer matches רבן גמליאל and goes against his own earlier ruling from Step 16. The גמרא does not explain why he said this here. This sets up רבן גמליאל's confrontation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21, but contradicts רבי יהושע's own answer in Step 16.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל confronts רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says he was told in רבי יהושע's name that the answer was yes, and orders him to stand while witnesses testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: But they told me in your name: yes! יהושע, stand on your feet, and they will testify against you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל challenges רבי יהושע's 'no' by pointing out that he had said 'yes' before. He orders him to stand so witnesses can testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not about logic. It is about what רבי יהושע really said. Making him stand is like putting a person on trial in front of everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: And they will testify against you

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him:
But surely they told me in your name: yes!
Yehoshua, stand on your feet,
and they will testify against you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 22 using the report from Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He had already ruled 'yes' to רבי צדוק, and witnesses can confirm it.

steps.title: רבי יהושע admits he cannot deny it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says that since רבי צדוק is alive, he cannot deny having said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע stood on his feet and said: What can I do? If I were alive and he were dead, the living could deny the dead. But now that I am alive and he is alive, how can the living deny the living?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע stands as ordered and admits that he did say it. He explains that he cannot deny something a living witness heard from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי צדוק were no longer alive, no one could contradict a denial. But רבי צדוק is right there and can testify. So רבי יהושע has to admit he gave that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: How should I act? (What can I do?)
If it were the case that...

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua stood on his feet and said:
What can I do?
If I were alive and he (Rabbi Tzadok) were dead,
the living could contradict the dead;
now that I am alive and he is alive,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ חַי יָכוֹל לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַחַי?
phrases.english: how can the living contradict the living?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיאַךְ חַי יָכוֹל לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the confrontation in Step 23 with an admission.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He admits that he did rule 'yes,' because the living witness can contradict a denial.

steps.title: רבי יהושע is left standing until the people protest
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל keeps teaching while רבי יהושע stands, until the people protest and tell the מתורגמן to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל kept standing and teaching, and רבי יהושע kept standing on his feet, until all the people murmured and said to חוצפית the מתורגמן: Stop! And he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The story describes what happened next. רבן גמליאל did not let רבי יהושע sit, and the crowd protested by stopping the lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halachic question is now finished. The story moves to how רבי יהושע was treated. The people saw it as disrespectful, so they told the מתורגמן to stop passing on רבן גמליאל's words.

keyTerms.meaning: חוצפית the announcer, who repeated the lecture out loud to the crowd

steps.confusionAlert: The final 'עֲמוֹד' does NOT mean 'stand up' here. It means 'stop!' The people told the מתורגמן to stop repeating the lecture, and 'וְעָמַד' means he stopped.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע had ruled that a חבר is believed, and רבן גמליאל disagreed. When confronted, רבי יהושע admitted his ruling. רבן גמליאל left him standing, and the people protested.

phrases.english: And Rabban Gamliel was standing and lecturing,
and Rabbi Yehoshua was standing on his feet,
until all the people murmured
and said to Chutzpit the announcer:
Stop! And he stopped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the result of the confrontation in Steps 23 and 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: the crowd protested רבי יהושע's humiliation by halting רבן גמליאל's lecture.

steps.title: The משנה: a כהן is believed that an expert saw the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a כהן is believed when he says he showed a בכור to an expert and it was found to be a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A כהן is believed to say: 'I showed this firstborn animal to an expert, and it is blemished.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It says a כהן is believed when he claims an expert already checked this בכור and ruled it has a real blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy בכור is holy and may not be eaten outside the מקדש. Once an expert rules it has a permanent blemish, the כהן may eat it anywhere. The משנה trusts the כהן's report that this ruling already happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn male animal, given to a כהן
Blemished animal, which may be eaten outside the מקדש

phrases.english: MISHNAH
The priest is believed to say:
"I showed this firstborn [to an expert]
phrases.notes: The word 'expert' is implied. Only an expert can rule that a blemish is permanent.

phrases.english: and it is blemished."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is believed to claim that an expert already ruled his בכור blemished.

steps.title: רב: a כהן is believed that he received the firstborn already blemished
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a כהן is believed to say a ישראל gave him the בכור already blemished. The reason is that people do not lie about something that can easily come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A כהן is believed to say, 'A ישראל gave me this בכור with its blemish already on it.' Why? People do not lie about something that is likely to come out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a new case. A כהן says the blemish was already there when the ישראל gave him the animal, and רב says we believe him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים are suspected of making blemishes on their own בכורות so they can eat them. Here, though, the כהן's claim can easily be checked by asking the ישראל who gave it. A person will not tell a lie that is so easy to expose.

keyTerms.meaning: Likely to be revealed or found out
People do not lie about it

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of מילתא דעבידא לאיגלויי (people do not lie about what can be checked) is used all over ש״ס. It is the main topic of the rest of this sugya.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
The priest is believed to say
"An Israelite gave me this firstborn with its blemish [already on it]."
What is the reason?
Any matter that is likely to be revealed,
people do not lie about it.
phrases.notes: Anyone can simply ask the ישראל whether this is true.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case to the משנה's topic of believing a כהן about a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is believed to say the בכור was given to him already blemished, because people do not lie about things that can be found out.

steps.title: רב אשי tries to prove רב's rule from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says our משנה already teaches רב's rule. The כהן is believed about the expert's ruling because the expert can be asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We also learned this in our משנה. 'A כהן is believed to say: I showed this בכור to an expert and it is blemished.' Why is he believed? Isn't it because people do not lie about something likely to come out?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support for רב from our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the claim about the expert could be checked by asking the expert, and the כהן is believed. רב אשי argues that this must be the same logic of מילתא דעבידא לאיגלויי that רב used.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned (this) in a משנה
Is it not because…? (introduces a proposed reason)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We too have learned [this]:
The priest is believed to say
"I showed this firstborn [to an expert] and it is blemished."
What is the reason?
Is it not because we say
any matter that is likely to be revealed,
people do not lie about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב's rule from step 26.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that a כהן is believed because his claim could be checked
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, which believes the כהן about the expert's ruling

steps.title: Rejection: the משנה trusts the כהן for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In the משנה the כהן is trusted because he would not eat קדשים outside the מקדש. In רב's case, כהנים are suspected about blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, in the משנה, the reason he is believed is that a כהן would not eat קדשים outside the מקדש. But here, in רב's case, since כהנים are suspected of making blemishes, they are also suspected of lying about how the blemish got there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי's proof. It shows the משנה can be explained without the rule of things that can be found out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a healthy, unblemished בכור outside the מקדש is a sin a כהן would not commit. So we trust him that an expert permitted it. But כהנים are known to be suspected of causing blemishes, so we have no reason to trust their story about where a blemish came from. The משנה therefore does not prove רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy offerings eaten outside the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This rejection does not say רב is wrong. It only says the משנה cannot serve as proof for רב, because the משנה can be explained a different way.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּקָדָשִׁים בְּחוּץ לָא אָכֵיל,
phrases.english: There, [the reason] is that he would not eat sacred meat outside [the Temple];
but here,
since they are suspected [of making blemishes], they are suspected [of lying about it too].
phrases.notes: כהנים are suspected of making a blemish themselves and then claiming it was already there.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם הוּא דְּקָדָשִׁים בְּחוּץ לָא אָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה. רב's ruling itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה has a different reason: a כהן will not eat קדשים outside the מקדש. That reason does not apply to רב's case, where כהנים are suspected about blemishes.

steps.title: רב שיזבי challenges רב from the case of מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי quotes a משנה in דמאי. An untrustworthy agent is not believed that he bought produce from a reliable seller, even though that could be checked. This seems to go against רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי objected: Someone says to a person who is not trusted about מעשר, 'Buy for me from someone who is trusted,' or 'from someone who separates מעשר.' The agent is not believed. Why not? We should say that people do not lie about something likely to come out!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי attacks רב's principle using a משנה from מסכת דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether the agent really bought from a trusted seller can easily be checked by asking the seller. Even so, the משנה does not believe the agent. This seems to show that 'people do not lie about what can come out' is not a reliable rule, which contradicts רב.

phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹמֵר לְמִי שֶׁאֵין נֶאֱמָן עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר
phrases.english: One who says to someone who is not trusted regarding tithes:
"Buy for me from someone who is trusted,"
or "from someone who tithes":
he [the agent] is not believed.
Why?
Let us say: any matter that is likely to be revealed,
people do not lie about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof was rejected, the גמרא now challenges רב's rule directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's principle that people do not lie about things likely to come out (step 27)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The agent's claim could be checked by asking the seller, yet the משנה in דמאי does not believe him. This contradicts רב's principle.

steps.title: The case there is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to defend רב by saying the דמאי case from רב שיזבי is different from רב's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to answer רב שיזבי's question. It says the דמאי case is different, and the next words will explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שיזבי argued that the דמאי case shows people are not trusted even when their claim can be checked. The גמרא answers that the דמאי case has some special feature, so it does not disprove רב's rule. The actual difference is not stated on this amud. It comes at the start of the next amud (36b).

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. Used to show that a proof's case is not like the case being discussed.
There. Here it refers to the case in the דמאי משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the opening of the answer. Do not stop here and think the question is fully answered. The reason for the difference comes next.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the דמאי case that רב שיזבי quoted. This formula opens an answer that sets the source apart from the case being discussed.
